Preparation
prep-a-RAY-shun
n.
From Latin praeparatio, from prae (before) and parare (to make ready). Webster 1828: the act of preparing or fitting a thing for use; previous measures of readiness. Paul makes it a piece of armour, and Proverbs traces it back to God.

Biblical Definition

Among the pieces of the whole armour of God, the footwear is the one most often passed over: your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace (Ephesians 6:15). The soldier’s sandal is not a weapon; it is what lets him stand his ground and go where he is sent, and the readiness supplied is the gospel of peace — a man at peace with God can be sent anywhere. Proverbs traces even the inward act of preparing to its source: The preparations of the heart in man, and the answer of the tongue, is from the LORD (Proverbs 16:1). Not merely the outcome but the readying itself is God’s work, which is why the same chapter can command a man to commit his works unto the LORD and promise that his thoughts shall be established. The word also names a day. The Gospels mark the timing of the burial by it: when the even was come, because it was the preparation, that is, the day before the sabbath (Mark 15:42) — the day on which Israel got ready for rest, and on which the Lord of the sabbath was laid in a tomb. John the Baptist’s whole office was this word in a person: Prepare ye the way of the LORD (Isaiah 40:3).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines PREPARATION as the act of preparing or fitting a thing for a particular use; previous measures of adaptation; the state of being prepared or in readiness.

expand to see more

PREPARATION, n. — The act or operation of preparing or fitting a thing for a particular purpose or use.

Previous measures of adaptation; as, preparations for war.

The state of being prepared or in readiness; as, a man in preparation for the event.

That which is prepared; something made or compounded for a particular purpose.

Latin praeparatio, from prae, before, and paro, to make ready — the root of repair and apparatus.

Key Scripture

Ephesians 6:15 — "And your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace;"

Proverbs 16:1 — "The preparations of the heart in man, and the answer of the tongue, is from the LORD."

Mark 15:42 — "And now when the even was come, because it was the preparation, that is, the day before the sabbath,"

Isaiah 40:3 — "The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God."

Modern Corruption

Proverbs 16:1 assigns even the inward preparing of the heart to the LORD, which is precisely the point at which synergistic accounts of conversion must qualify the text.

expand to see more

The preparations of the heart in man... is from the LORD. If the readying of the heart is God’s, then the decisive movement in conversion is not the sinner’s. This is the doctrine of effectual calling: the Spirit does not merely make salvation available and wait, He renews the will and thereby makes the sinner willing, so that the man comes freely and comes certainly. Arminian and semi-Pelagian accounts must at this point make the preparation a cooperative act in which the final determination rests with the creature, and the text will not divide that way — it says the preparations are from the LORD, without remainder. Philippians 2:13 states the same thing positively: it is God which worketh in you both to will and to do of His good pleasure. The believer’s effort is real, commanded, and strenuous; it is not the origin of itself.

Ephesians 6:15 deserves rescue from a common misreading that turns the shoes into a duty to evangelize. The genitive is better taken as the readiness that the gospel of peace supplies: a man who is at peace with God is thereby made able to stand. That order matters pastorally. Believers are regularly exhorted to be bold, ready, and immovable, as though these were qualities to be summoned; Paul roots them in an accomplished peace they already possess through justification (Romans 5:1). Mark 15:42 sets the darkest instance of the word in the calendar: on the day appointed for getting ready to rest, the body of the Lord of the sabbath was laid in a borrowed tomb, and the true rest was being prepared in a way none of them yet understood.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek hetoimasia (G2091), readiness, preparation; paraskeue (G3904), the preparation day before the sabbath; Hebrew maarak (H4633), an arrangement or ordering; kun (H3559), to establish or make ready.

expand to see more

Greek hetoimasia (G2091) — readiness, preparedness; the preparation of the gospel of peace (Ephesians 6:15).

Greek paraskeue (G3904) — the day of preparation, the eve of the sabbath (Mark 15:42).

Hebrew maarak (H4633) — an arrangement, an ordering of thought; the preparations of the heart (Proverbs 16:1).

Hebrew kun (H3559) — to set upright, to establish, to make ready; the standing verb behind a heart prepared toward God.

Hebrew panah (H6437) — to turn, to clear a way; Prepare ye the way of the LORD (Isaiah 40:3).

Usage

"Your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace (Ephesians 6:15) — a man at peace with God can be sent anywhere."

"The preparations of the heart in man... is from the LORD (Proverbs 16:1) — not merely the outcome but the readying."

"Because it was the preparation, that is, the day before the sabbath (Mark 15:42) — the Lord of the sabbath laid in a tomb on the day of getting ready."
